Attach logical assertions to control-flow edges and verify local correctness conditions that ensure global safety.

histories.work: An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming
histories.claim: Logical proof rules for program properties; a verified finite invariant is a small mechanical proof instance.

candidate.arguments: (states:finite ordered identities, initials:set of these states, invariant:set of these states, transitions:set of ordered edges among these states). Complete explicit finite transition relation: every possible transition must be included.
candidate.behavior: Return either {valid: YES} exactly when initials subset invariant AND for every transition (s,t) whose source s is inside invariant, t is also inside invariant; or return {valid:NO, reason: INITIAL-OUTSIDE, witness: smallest initial state outside invariant}; else {valid:NO, reason: ESCAPING-EDGE, witness: lexicographically smallest (s,t) with s inside invariant and t outside}. State IDs sorted by exact code-point order only for deterministic evidence. This is an inductive proof certificate, not a general reachability result, no program execution and no proof of termination.
candidate.epistemic_boundary: An inductive invariant suffices to prove all reachable states safe under a complete transition graph, but may fail even when all actually reachable states are safe due to an unreachable state inside I with an escaping edge. All concrete source states must be known and fully enumerated: missing transitions invalidate any extrapolation to real CPU/FPGA. The oracle validates the provided finite model only.
falsifiers: Reject as invalid an invariant that contains an unreachable state with an escaping edge: reachable safety does not imply inductiveness.
Return the wrong smallest violating state/edge when multiple witnesses exist.
Ignore an initial state outside the invariant.
Treat lack of termination evidence as a termination proof.
Accept an edge referencing a state outside the explicitly declared finite state universe.
Claim this single finite instance proves the behavior of a real MCU/scheduler/FPGA without complete state modeling.

dedup_neighbors.d1_d9: Ratified D1–D9 has predicates, equality, finite data and control semantics, but exact named finite inductiveness certificate not found at snapshot; complete behavior comparison remains pending.
dedup_neighbors.core_vs_library: This can be implemented using finite set comparisons, but it is a distinct language-visible certificate relation, not merely an optimization/index or hardware opcode. DERIVABLE is not automatic EXCLUDE, but owner must decide if a 10-bit resident is justified.
